title: Annual Financial Review: 6 Checks Beyond Mutual Funds
description: Financial planning is comprehensive and extends far beyond just investing in mutual funds. Annually reviewing six key areas ensures your financial strategy re.

faq.q: Why is an annual financial review important?
faq.a: An annual review ensures your financial plan stays aligned with your evolving life goals, risk tolerance, and economic conditions. It helps identify gaps, optimise resources, and protect your wealth proactively.

faq.q: How often should I review my insurance policies?
faq.a: You should review your insurance policies annually, or immediately after any significant life event such as marriage, childbirth, taking a new loan, or a change in dependents.

faq.q: What documents do I need for an estate plan?
faq.a: Key documents for estate planning include a Will, nominations for all assets (bank accounts, investments, insurance), and potentially a Power of Attorney.

faq.q: Can I do tax planning throughout the year?
faq.a: Yes, tax planning is most effective when done throughout the year, rather than just at the financial year-end. This allows for better decision-making regarding investments and expenditures to optimise tax savings.

faq.q: Should I only focus on returns during my investment review?
faq.a: No, while returns are important, you should also consider asset allocation, risk levels, diversification, expense ratios, and the tax implications of your investments.

faq.q: What if I have too many loans?
faq.a: If you have multiple high-interest loans, consider strategies like debt consolidation or prioritising prepayment of the most expensive loans to reduce your overall interest burden.

faq.q: Is a nominee the same as a legal heir?
faq.a: No, a nominee is a custodian who receives the assets on behalf of the legal heirs. The legal heir, as per a Will or succession laws, is the ultimate owner of the assets.
